attrs.management_says: Gross margin expansion due to favorable channel mix: higher direct-to-consumer (DTC) proportion, lower international distributor sales.
attrs.numbers_show: DSO improved from 60 to 58 days; receivables grew 8.0% vs revenue 10.7%. This aligns with a shift to DTC (cash/credit-card sales) away from wholesale/distributor channels that generate receivables.

attrs.management_says: Revenue growth led by Columbia brand, prAna acquisition (~$56M incremental for first five months of 2015), Sorel brand, and favorable channel mix shift to direct-to-consumer (E36, E37, E38).
attrs.numbers_show: Revenue grew 10.7% ($225.6M) to $2,326.2M. prAna incremental $56M accounts for ~25% of growth. Gross margin expanded to 46.1% from 45.5%, consistent with higher DTC mix (E12, E23, E37). Quarterly growth strong in Q1-Q3 (+12.9% to +17.3%) but slowed to +3.3% in Q4 (E25-E28).

attrs.management_says: No explicit explanation for 2015 receivables movement in evidence; general references to seasonality and ERP implementation (E30, E49).
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 8.0% ($27.6M) vs revenue +10.7%; DSO improved from 60 to 58 days (E23). Quarterly: Q1 AR +1% (DSO 53→48), Q2 AR -3% (DSO 57→47), Q3 AR +15.5% (DSO 62→63), Q4 AR +8% (DSO 46→48) (E25-E28). Pattern shows AR growing slower than revenue overall, consistent with healthy demand.

attrs.management_says: Revenue grew 11% (15% constant-currency) led by Columbia brand, prAna brand ($56M incremental for first five months of 2015), and Sorel brand, partially offset by Mountain Hardwear decline (E33, E36).
attrs.numbers_show: Revenue rose $225.6M (10.7%) to $2,326.2M (E1, E12, E23). prAna acquired May 30, 2014; the cited $56M for Jan–May 2015 represents ~25% of total growth, a timing/acquisition effect visible in the year-over-year comparison (E36).

attrs.management_says: No explanation for 2015 receivables or operating cash flow movements is present in the provided MD&A excerpts. The only cash flow discussion (E47) covers 2014 vs 2013.
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 8% ($344.4M → $372.0M) while revenue grew 10.7%; DSO improved 60→58 days annually (E7, E18, E23). But quarterly signals show Q3 receivables +15.5% vs revenue +13.7% (DSO 62→63) and Q4 receivables +8.0% vs revenue +3.3% (DSO 46→48), indicating late-year shipment timing (E27, E28). Operating cash flow fell 49% ($185.8M → $95.1M) while net income rose 27% ($137.2M → $174.3M) (E5, E6, E16, E17, E24).

attrs.management_says: Gross margin expansion driven by favorable channel mix (higher DTC, lower international distributor sales) (E38).
attrs.numbers_show: Gross margin improved 45.5%→46.1% (implied from E37). The shift to DTC (higher margin, faster cash collection) and away from distributors (lower margin, longer terms) is consistent with stable/improving annual DSO despite Q3/Q4 deterioration.

attrs.reason: The channel mix shift (higher DTC, lower distributor) is stated in MD&A (E38) but no reported numbers in the pack show the channel mix proportions or their change; DSO improvement (E23) is consistent with but not proof of the shift.

attrs.reason: Management attributes revenue growth to Columbia brand, prAna acquisition (~$56M incremental), Sorel brand, and a channel mix shift to direct-to-consumer. The evidence pack provides total revenue (E12), quarterly revenue (E25-E28), gross margin expansion (E37), and MD&A statements (E36, E37, E38) that quantify the prAna incremental ($56M) and note product category growth. However, brand-level (Columbia, Sorel) and channel-level (DTC vs wholesale) revenue breakdowns are not present as reported numbers (XBRL facts or MD&A figures). The only quantified driver is the prAna figure, which is itself a management claim. The other named drivers are not visible in the numbers, so the explanation rests largely on management's word.
